{
  "summary": "Save reindexing progress upon interruption so that a restarted node resumes from the last completed block file instead of restarting from blk00000.dat. The last completed block file number and the in-memory orphan block positions are persisted to the block tree database when an interrupt is signaled. Once all block files are processed, the reindex flag and progress checkpoints are erased in an atomic, synced database write.",
  "problem": "When a node reindex is interrupted by shutdown or a crash, or if interrupted during chain activation before reindex completion is flushed, the next startup restarts the reindex from the very first block file (blk00000.dat), discarding hours or days of indexing work.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'Currently, if the reindex process is interrupted it will start over on next run at blk00000.dat. Even after reindexing is finished when the node is in ActivateBestChain() an interruption may STILL require a full reindex process because DB_REINDEX_FLAG is written false, but not flushed.'"

result.summary: Save reindexing progress upon interruption so that a restarted node resumes from the last completed block file instead of restarting from blk00000.dat. The last completed block file number and the in-memory orphan block positions are persisted to the block tree database when an interrupt is signaled. Once all block files are processed, the reindex flag and progress checkpoints are erased in an atomic, synced database write.
result.problem: When a node reindex is interrupted by shutdown or a crash, or if interrupted during chain activation before reindex completion is flushed, the next startup restarts the reindex from the very first block file (blk00000.dat), discarding hours or days of indexing work.
evidence: PR description: 'Currently, if the reindex process is interrupted it will start over on next run at blk00000.dat. Even after reindexing is finished when the node is in ActivateBestChain() an interruption may STILL require a full reindex process because DB_REINDEX_FLAG is written false, but not flushed.'
result.scope_notes: Touches blockstorage database schema with two new key types for reindex checkpointing and adds a functional test case to feature_reindex.py.
result.card: Allows interrupted reindex operations to resume from the last completed block file rather than restarting from the beginning. When an interrupt is detected during reindexing, the node persists the last completed block file index along with the serialized orphan block map to the block tree database, and atomically clears all reindex state with a synced write once complete. This avoids discarding hours or days of reindexing work if a node is stopped or interrupted before completion.
